top_story_title: SonicWall SMA1000: maximum-severity flaw CVE-2026-102255 exploited three days after the patch
top_story_summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-102255, a maximum-severity vulnerability in SonicWall SMA1000 remote-access appliances. SonicWall patched it on Tuesday; exploitation was reported three days later. The source does not state a fixed build number, so confirm the target release against the SonicWall advisory before scheduling the upgrade.
top_actions: Inventory all SMA1000 appliances and record the running build; compare it against the fixed release in SonicWall's advisory for CVE-2026-102255 (the reporting does not name a build number).
Apply the vendor fixed build now rather than at the next window - exploitation is already reported and the appliance is internet-facing by design.
Terminate all active sessions and revoke session tokens after the upgrade; assume session cookies were stolen during the pre-patch window.
Rotate appliance admin credentials, service-account passwords, certificates and any secrets stored on the SMA1000.

Hunt for compromise before closing the ticket: new or modified local accounts, unexpected outbound connections from the appliance, altered web resources, and anomalous timestamps in the appliance logs.
executive_summary: SonicWall SMA1000: CVE-2026-102255, maximum severity, under active exploitation three days after the patch shipped. Patch, then rotate credentials and kill sessions - the upgrade alone does not evict a pre-patch intruder.
No fixed build number appears in the reporting for CVE-2026-102255; take the target release from SonicWall's advisory, not from secondary coverage.

Four more U.S. states (Florida, Iowa, Montana, Nebraska) sued TP-Link Systems on October 6 over router security and China-ties claims, bringing the total to five. No vulnerability, no action on the devices - a procurement and supply-chain-risk signal only.
Nothing AI-related in this window; the site carries forward the previous AI section.
key_actions: **SonicWall** — Identify every SMA1000 appliance and its running build from the asset inventory, including units in DR sites and in HA pairs.

**SonicWall** — Apply the SonicWall fixed build for CVE-2026-102255; take the target version from the vendor advisory, as public reporting states only that a patch shipped and not which release carries it.

headlines.title: Max severity SonicWall SMA1000 flaw now exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: A maximum-severity flaw in SonicWall SMA1000 remote-access appliances, CVE-2026-102255, is being exploited in attacks three days after the patch shipped.

headlines.title: TP-Link Sued by Four More U.S. States Over Router Security and China Ties
headlines.summary: Florida, Iowa, Montana and Nebraska sued TP-Link Systems on October 6 over its router security and China-independence claims, bringing the state suits to five.
